function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity as a phenomenon has been known since antiquity (e.g., static electricity from amber), but its systematic study began in the 17th–18th centuries. Key figures include William Gilbert (who coined the term “electricus”), Benjamin Franklin (famous for his kite experiment), Alessandro Volta (invented the voltaic pile), and later scientists like Michael Faraday and James Clerk Maxwell who developed the laws governing electromagnetism. So while no single person “discovered” electricity, it was gradually uncovered and understood through contributions from many pioneers.
